#MachineLearning #GameDev #NLP #ComputerVision  
Jun Watanabe | Machine Learning Engineer at NexaGame Studios  

I build systems that make games smarter—whether it’s crafting AI that learns from player behavior or designing tools that let developers iterate faster. My work bridges the gap between data and creativity, turning raw numbers into experiences that stick.  

At NexaGame, I’ve focused on making gameplay more engaging. For example, I developed NLP models that power in-game dialogue, letting characters adapt to player choices in real time. That required balancing accuracy with speed, which meant optimizing models for low-latency inference—something I’ve fine-tuned using PyTorch and REST APIs.  

Computer vision has been a key part of my toolkit too. Recently, I built a system to analyze player movements in multiplayer matches, helping refine character controls. It’s the kind of work where small tweaks in model architecture can make a big difference.  

I also spend time ensuring models run smoothly in production. With Kubernetes and Docker, I’ve streamlined deployment pipelines, and MLOps tools like MLflow have made tracking experiments feel less like a chore. Cloud costs? I’ve kept them in check by prioritizing efficiency without sacrificing performance.  

When I’m not coding, I’m thinking about how to make tech feel less technical. After all, the best systems are the ones players never notice—until they can’t imagine the game without them.
